header.title: Monty IFC Viewer
header.heroAlt: Monty IFC Viewer: a timber house halfway through the construction sequence; built parts in colour, the next phase in orange and the rest transparent, with the player at the bottom
header.label: BIM and IFC viewer
header.tagline: Show your client the construction sequence, with a single link
header.desc: Open a shared model in the browser, on your computer, tablet or phone. Play back the assembly order phase by phase, filter by mark or type, and look inside the building with a section box.

meta.description: Free IFC viewer in the browser that plays back the construction sequence. Share a link to your model and show your client, phase by phase, how the building goes up, with filters, a section box and an exploded view. Also as a desktop app for Windows, macOS and Linux.
meta.title: Monty IFC Viewer — OpenAEC Foundation

sequence.alt: Construction sequence in night mode: placed parts grey, the element with mark 303 orange and the rest of the building transparent
sequence.title: Show how the building goes up
sequence.desc: Play back the assembly, or step through the model phase by phase with the slider. What is already in place keeps its colour, the current phase lights up orange and what is still to come is transparent. The order comes from each element's mark number.

filter.alt: Filter panel with mark ranges 100–199 and 300–399 ticked; only those elements are shown in colour, the rest is transparent
filter.title: See only what you need
filter.desc: Look up an element by mark number, or tick mark ranges and element types. The rest of the model turns transparent, so you can see where those parts are.

section.alt: Section box around the model, moved down to the floor level with the walls cut through
section.title: Look inside the building
section.desc: Put a section box around the model and move its faces with the arrows. Take off a storey and see the layout and the walls underneath.

explode.alt: Exploded view: the wall and floor elements of the house pulled slightly apart, with the slider at the bottom
explode.title: Pull the model apart
explode.desc: The exploded view moves all elements apart, as far as you choose. Ideal for showing which parts make up a prefab or timber project.

select.alt: A beam under the house is clicked and shown in light blue; on the right the panel with its name, mark 147 and the Isolate, Hide and Reset buttons
select.title: Click a part and set it apart
select.desc: Tap an element to see its name and mark number. Isolate or hide it with one button, or select several at once, also with a tap on a tablet.

player.title: Play and step
player.desc: Play, pause, previous and next phase, or jump to a phase with the slider.

speed.title: Your own pace
speed.desc: Choose two seconds down to a quarter of a second per phase.

ghost.title: Done, in progress, to do
ghost.desc: Placed parts in their own colour, the current phase orange, the rest transparent.

mark.title: Order from the mark number
mark.desc: Reads the mark from the IFC properties or from Revit, including the CLT marks of timber elements.

section.title: Section box
section.desc: Cut the model on six sides and move or rotate the box.

explode.title: Exploded view
explode.desc: Pull the elements apart with a slider.

measure.title: Measuring
measure.desc: Distance, perpendicular distance and area, also on a tablet.

theme.title: Day and night
theme.desc: A light or dark view, with one button.

zoom.title: Zoom and reset
zoom.desc: Zoom to the whole model, or reset section, measurements and explode in one go.

click.title: Click an element
click.desc: See its name and mark number, and isolate or hide the element.

multi.title: Several elements at once
multi.desc: With Ctrl or Shift, or with the multi-select button on a tablet.

menu.title: Right-click menu
menu.desc: Isolate, hide and reset from a menu.

filters.title: Filter by mark and type
filters.desc: Search for a mark number, or choose mark ranges per hundred and element types.

link.title: One link per project
link.desc: Your client opens the model without installing or uploading anything.

overview.title: Project overview
overview.desc: A start page per client with a preview, phase and location per project, search and filtering by type.

models.title: Several models per project

mobile.title: Tablet and phone

whatsnew.label: New in v1.0.1
whatsnew.title: The viewer on your own computer
whatsnew.desc: Version 1.0 is the desktop app for Windows, macOS and Linux. Open IFC files from your own computer without sharing them first.

files.a: IFC models from any BIM program, such as Revit, Archicad or Tekla. The web version shows models stored on the Speckle server: as an uploaded IFC file or sent straight from Revit with the Speckle connector. The desktop app opens IFC files from your own computer.

install.q: Do I need to install anything?
install.a: No. Anyone with a link opens the model straight in the browser, also on a tablet or phone. To open your own IFC files without sharing them, install the desktop app.

price.q: What does Monty IFC Viewer cost?
price.a: Nothing. Viewing is free and needs no account, and the source code is public on GitHub.

systems.q: Which systems does it run on?
systems.a: The web version runs in any modern browser, on computer, tablet and phone. The desktop app is available for Windows (.exe and .msi), macOS on Apple Silicon (.dmg) and Linux (.deb, .rpm and AppImage).

practice.a: Yes. It works with IFC, the open standard for BIM, and takes the order from the mark number you already fill in in Revit or in the IFC properties. For timber construction it also reads the marks of CLT elements.

own.q: How do I put my own model in the web version?
own.a: The model goes onto OpenAEC's Speckle server, as an IFC upload or from Revit. The project then gets its own link and a place on your client's project page. Contact us to set this up.

drop.q: Can I open an IFC file straight in the web version?
drop.a: Not yet. The web version shows shared models from the server. For a single file from your own computer, use the desktop app.

props.q: Can I see all properties of an element?
props.a: Not yet for IFC models in the web version: there the panel shows the name and the mark number. For models sent straight from Revit you also see the parameters per group.

difference.q: What is the difference between the web version and the desktop app?
difference.a: The web version is made for sharing: a link, a project overview, measuring, section box and filters, and it works on a tablet. The desktop app (version 1.0) opens single IFC files from your own computer and colours elements by a parameter.
